models.inverse_notes: Forward maps (m, s) to K. Inverse to mass: m = 2K/s^2 requires s != 0; the admitted s = 0 boundary (with K = 0) leaves m underdetermined. Inverse to speed: s^2 = 2K/m gives formal roots s = +/-sqrt(2K/m); because s is a speed, only the nonnegative root is admissible, requiring m > 0 (strict; the m = 0 boundary is excluded from inversion) and K >= 0. Substitution check: K = 4000 J with m = 80 kg gives s = sqrt(2*4000/80) = sqrt(100) = 10 m/s, matching the athlete reference. Causal invertibility is not claimed: K alone does not determine direction of motion.
limitations: Excludes relativistic speeds; use the deferred relativistic form when v approaches c.
Excludes rotational kinetic energy and deformable-body internal energy.
Zero mass is an admitted ideal boundary (gives K = 0) and does not describe a real classical particle.

models.inverse_notes: Forward maps (x0, v0, a, t) to x. Inverse to duration is quadratic: (a/2) t^2 + v0 t + (x0 - x) = 0. For a != 0, t = (-v0 +/- sqrt(v0^2 + 2a(x - x0))) / a; the discriminant must be nonnegative, and any negative root violates the t >= 0 guard and is excluded, which is the assignment's two-root check. Degenerate a = 0 reduces to linear t = (x - x0)/v0 requiring v0 != 0. Inverse to acceleration: a = 2(x - x0 - v0 t)/t^2 requires t != 0. Substitution check: dragster reference (x = 402, x0 = 0, v0 = 0, a = 26) gives t = sqrt(2*402/26) = sqrt(30.92) = 5.56 s, matching the published duration. Inversions to x0 and v0 are linear and were not numerically checked here.
limitations: Constant acceleration only; varying acceleration needs the deferred integral treatment.
One-dimensional motion with a fixed axis, origin and clock; rotating frames and frame changes excluded.
Position x is frame-dependent; only differences x - x0 are translation-invariant.

references.method: Source-reported result: the worked dragster example (from rest, 26.0 m/s^2, 5.56 s) states x = 402 m (0.5*26*5.56^2 = 401.88). Tolerance covers three-significant-figure rounding of published inputs and output.
Independently constructed inputs; cross-checked via the companion average-velocity form from the same section: v = 2 + 3*4 = 14, x = 1 + (2 + 14)/2*4 = 33. Exact small-integer arithmetic.

models.inverse_notes: Forward maps (m, g, dh) to dU. Inverse to height change: dh = dU/(m g) requires m > 0 and g > 0 strictly; the admitted ideal zeros (m = 0 or g = 0, giving dU = 0) leave dh underdetermined. Inverse to mass: m = dU/(g dh) requires g·dh != 0. Substitution check: dU = 108000 J with m = 75 kg and g = 9.8 m/s^2 gives dh = 108000/735 = 146.94 m, matching the published 147 m ascent. Inversion to g was not numerically checked here.
limitations: Uniform-field approximation only; height changes comparable to Earth radius need the general Newtonian form (deferred backlog).
Excludes the absolute zero reference: single-height values depend on an arbitrary datum, only differences are modeled.
Zero-mass and zero-field inputs are admitted ideal boundaries (giving dU = 0) and do not describe real gravitating systems.

references.method: Source-reported result: Example 8.2 (75-kg hiker ascending 147 m from the base) states 1.08e5 J relative to the base (75*9.8*147 = 108045). Tolerance covers three-significant-figure rounding of the published result.
Independently constructed inputs; regrouped as weight-times-height (2*9.81 = 19.62 N, times 3.0 m = 58.86 J) as an arithmetic consistency check.
Descending 147 m reverses the sign of the difference (75*9.8*(-147) = -108045), confirming signed semantics symmetric to the published ascent.

models.inverse_notes: Forward maps (F, d) to W. Inverse to force: F = W/d requires d != 0; W = 0 with d = 0 leaves F underdetermined. Inverse to displacement is symmetric. Sign analysis: W > 0 means the force assists the displacement; W < 0 (negative work) means it opposes it. Substitution check: W = 1535 J with d = 25.0 m gives F = 61.4 N, matching the lawn-mower component used in the reference. A power (rate-of-work) inversion needs a separate model and was not tested.
limitations: Collinear scope only: angled forces must first be projected to the displacement axis by the caller; the general angle form needs a trigonometric operator outside the v1 grammar.
Constant force only; varying forces need the deferred integral form.
With no guards, every finite signed pair is accepted; there is no domain rejection case, only a missing-input case.

references.method: Source-reported result: Example 7.1 (75.0 N at 35 degrees over 25.0 m) states W = 1.54e3 J. The model input is the force component along the displacement, F = 75.0*cos(35 deg) = 61.4 N, projected outside the tested expression (61.4*25 = 1535). Tolerance covers three-significant-figure rounding of the published result and inputs.

The projection F = F_full cos(theta) is the caller's responsibility and is demonstrated (not hidden) in the lawn-mower reference. No constants are inlined. Dimensional check: [F][d] = (M L/T^2)(L) = M L^2 T^-2 = J. Signed (not magnitude-only) semantics preserve negative work.
